subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?
body:
Bharat, all,
 
We've now discussed corporate credit turnaround time at every Wholesale Banki=g review since April. Before we go into the September MBR I want a straight, unvarnished a=swer rather than another incremental update.
 
Three questions:
1. What has actually changed on the ground since April?
2. What is still driving the delays?
3. Is ORION addressing the root cause, or are we improving the easy cases whi=e the hard ones stay
 stuck?
 
Bharat - over to you first for the overall picture, then I'd like Sameer and =eeraj to weigh in directly rather than through a single consolidated response.
 
R Subramaniakumar

Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

Bharat, all,
 
We've now discussed corporate credit turnaround time at every Wholesale Banki=g review since April. Before we go into the September MBR I want a straight, unvarnished a=swer rather than another incremental update.
 
Three questions:
1. What has actually changed on the ground since April?
2. What is still driving the delays?
3. Is ORION addressing the root cause, or are we improving the easy cases whi=e the hard ones stay
 stuck?
 
Bharat - over to you first for the overall picture, then I'd like Sameer and =eeraj to weigh in directly rather than through a single consolidated response.
 
R Subramaniakumar

=== Message 2 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-62b627ca5edb75f03995377e1824a452
Date: 18 August 2026 14:20
From: bharat.rungta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

Kumar,
 
Fair question - let me give the headline view and let Sameer and Neeraj go de=per on their sides.
 
What's changed: standard-case proposals have genuinely improved. We're at rou=hly 6.4 days network-wide against a 9.2 day baseline from April. That's real and it's sh=wing up in RM feedback too.
 
What hasn't moved: exception-flagged proposals are still taking 13+ days, bar=ly different from where we started. Since exceptions are a meaningful share of our corporate bo=k (higher-ticket, more structured deals skew this way), the average client-facing experience ha=n't improved as much as the headline number suggests.
 
On whether ORION is fixing the root cause - honestly, I think we've picked th= low-hanging fruit first, which was the right sequencing, but we haven't yet properly tackled wh= exception cases are slow. Sameer, Neeraj - your take?
 
Bharat

=== Message 3 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-242e52b697ee021a5d672fbd56b5aaa4
Date: 19 August 2026 10:05
From: sameer.kapoor@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

All,
 
From Credit's side - the 13.1 day exception-case figure is accurate as far as=our reporting goes, but I'd flag a caveat: a portion of exception cases are still tracked partly =utside the digital tool because the core banking integration for exception workflow isn't done y=t (Kavya's team is on this, targeting October). So the true end-to-end number for those cases may b= understated - we're not fully confident in it yet.
 
On root cause: exceptions exist because a proposal has a genuine policy devia=ion - collateral shortfall, structure outside standard product parameters, name already at gro=p exposure limits, etc. That review needs credit judgement and I don't think it should be sped u= just for the sake of a TAT number. What I do think can move is how fast we get a complete, clean f=le to start that review - which is more a documentation and process question than a credit-pol=cy one.
 
Sameer

=== Message 4 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-c3957a995be87447464ba28c2a1cadc7
Date: 19 August 2026 16:40
From: neeraj.bhatia@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

Kumar, all,
 
From the frontline: RMs will tell you the digital checklist has genuinely hel=ed on standard deals
- less back and forth, faster sign-off. But the minute a case gets flagged as=an exception, the checklist stops being useful and it's back to the old manual process. So RMs =eel like exception cases haven't changed at all, which honestly isn't far off what the numbers s=y.
 
I'll also say - and Sameer won't love this - we still think a meaningful chun= of what gets flagged as an "exception" is a technical/documentation gap rather than a genuine cred=t judgement call.
Would like us to actually look at this with data rather than going back and f=rth on impressions.
Adoption of the checklist tool itself is also patchy - stronger in our metro =eams, weaker elsewhere, for reasons I can dig into separately if useful.
 
Neeraj

=== Message 5 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-f89d3f78804fd5b17e1f9254ef0d6197
Date: 20 August 2026 11:15
From: kavya.iyer@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

All,
 
Quick update from the pilot/technology side to add to this.
 
Adoption of the digital checklist is at 61% across pilot branches as of now, =p from 58% at the August review - moving, but slower than I'd like, and Neeraj's point about the metro/non-metr= split is real and something we should quantify properly.
 
On exception cases specifically - Sameer's caveat above is important. Until t=e core banking exception-workflow integration is live (targeting October), we're tracking a =eaningful chunk of exception-case activity manually outside the system, which is exactly why I'd=treat the current
13.1 day figure as directional rather than fully reliable. Once that integrat=on lands we'll have a much cleaner, end-to-end view.
 
Kavya

=== Message 6 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-ab1851eed383d49a1026847f0f40bc87
Date: 20 August 2026 17:50
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

Thanks all - this is more useful than the last few MBR updates combined.
 
Follow-up, mainly for Amit: if exception cases have basically not moved since we started on this in April, I want to understand exactly where the 13+ days is actually going, sta=e by stage, not just "policy checks take time." Can you get us an honest breakdown - genuine risk =eview time vs documentation rework vs simple queueing/routing delay?
 
I'd rather have an uncomfortable answer now than another quarter of the same =umber.
 
R Subramaniakumar

=== Message 7 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-d6d8c4f5669cf529b9ff35f8b2af1bcb
Date: 2026-09-16T21:49:48+00:00
From: tchourishi@alvarezandmarsal.com
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

From: Sameer Kapoor sameer.kapoor@rbl.bank.in
Sent: 21 August 2026 15:30
To: R Subramaniakumar r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in; Bharat Rungta bharat.rungta@rbl.bank.in
Cc: Neeraj Bhatia neeraj.bhatia@rbl.bank.in; Rohan Desai rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in; Kavya Iyer kavya.iyer@rbl.bank.in; Amit Sethi amit.sethi@rbl.bank.in
Subject: RE: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?
 
All,
 
Fair - Amit's numbers are more precise than what I had, and I accept the docu=entation-rework share is bigger than the "policy needs judgement" argument accounts for. I'm =ot going to defend
13 days on that basis.
 
Where I'd land: the risk-review time (4.2 days) is largely irreducible withou= a policy change we haven't discussed. The rework and queueing time (9+ days combined) is fair ga=e and is really a process and resourcing question, not a credit-policy one.
 
Suggest Credit, Credit Ops and Transformation jointly bring a specific plan t= the September MBR - not another adoption target, but a concrete proposal to cut documentation rew=rk and queueing time for exception cases. We already owe the MBR a Phase 2 rollout plan from July;=we'll fold this into the same submission.
 
Sameer

=== Message 8 of 8 ===
Message-ID: pg-868178aff5cd4409e806248e80ad12e7
Date: 21 August 2026 09:40
From: amit.sethi@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Corporate Credit TAT - where do we actually stand?

Kumar, all,
 
Pulled this together from the last full quarter of exception cases (network-w=de, n=126). Average elapsed time on an exception case is 13.4 days, breaking down roughly as:
 
- Genuine risk / credit review time: ~4.2 days
- Documentation rework and back-and-forth with the RM: ~5.5 days
- Queued awaiting manual routing/assignment (no one actively working it): ~3.= days
 
So documentation rework and idle queue time together are almost 70% of the el=psed time - the actual credit judgement piece Sameer is protecting is less than a third of th= total. I'd read this
as: the "exceptions need manual judgement" argument is valid, but it doesn't =xplain most of the 13 days.
 
Happy to share the full workings if useful.
 
Amit

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

Pipeline held steady at Rs 3,750 Cr across 46 accounts. Sanctions for March closed at Rs 1,020 Cr, the strongest month this fiscal year, largely on the back of two large renewable-energy facilities.

2. Corporate Underwriting Modernisation - Project ORION

Following the diagnostic commissioned in February, the group formally approved launch of the corporate underwriting modernisation initiative, internally named Project ORION. The diagnostic confirmed that policy-exception handling and manual documentation checks together account for the majority of elapsed TAT beyond the credit committee's own decisioning time.

Pilot scope: 5 branches - Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Ahmedabad corporate banking teams.

Baseline captured for pilot branches: standard-case TAT 9.5 days; exception-case TAT 15.2 days.

Target: reduce pilot-branch standard-case TAT to 6 days within the pilot window (target date: June 2026).

Kavya Iyer appointed pilot owner; Sameer Kapoor and Amit Sethi as credit/operations sponsors.

Scope includes a digital document checklist, auto-validation of standard financial covenants, and a revised exception-routing workflow.

3. Discussion

Kavya Iyer flagged that pilot success will depend heavily on RM adoption of the new digital checklist tool, which requires a change in how proposals are first logged.

Neeraj Bhatia asked that the pilot branches be given adequate training lead time before go-live metrics are judged.

Rohan Desai asked for exception-routing logic to be reviewed by Risk before go-live to ensure no policy checks are silently dropped.

4. Decisions

Project ORION pilot approved for go-live from 20 April 2026 in the five nominated branches.

Risk to sign off on exception-routing logic prior to go-live.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Full underwriting bottleneck diagnostic findings - detailed report circulated separately (closed as a standing item; findings incorporated into ORION scope above).

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

The wholesale pipeline improved to Rs 3,600 Cr across 44 accounts (Jan: Rs 3,200 Cr / 40 accounts), driven largely by renewed activity in the infrastructure and light manufacturing segments. Sanctions for the month stood at Rs 890 Cr against a target of Rs 950 Cr.

2. Credit Turnaround Time (TAT)

Average TAT for standard corporate proposals was 9.4 days against the internal target of 6 days (Jan: 9.6 days). Sameer Kapoor noted the improvement is marginal and not yet statistically meaningful. Approximately 18% of proposals were returned to the originating RM at least once for documentation rework, which the group agreed is a material contributor to elapsed TAT.

3. Discussion

Neeraj Bhatia flagged that RM teams are spending disproportionate time re-collating financial statements and KYC annexures rather than on credit structuring itself.

Amit Sethi presented a preliminary breakdown showing exception-flagged proposals take nearly 60% longer than clean proposals end-to-end.

Rohan Desai cautioned against diluting policy checks purely to compress TAT; asked that any diagnostic separate genuine risk-driven delay from process friction.

Group agreed a formal diagnostic of underwriting bottlenecks is required before deciding on any technology or process intervention.

4. Decisions

Commission a structured TAT diagnostic covering the last two quarters of proposals, to be jointly led by Credit and Credit Operations.

Neeraj Bhatia to nominate two RM teams (one metro, one non-metro) for a time-and-motion study.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Root-cause analysis of credit TAT (raised in January MBR) - in progress, folded into the new diagnostic exercise.

Digitisation options paper for corporate underwriting - deferred to March, pending diagnostic findings.

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

Pipeline held steady at Rs 3,750 Cr across 46 accounts. Sanctions for March closed at Rs 1,020 Cr, the strongest month this fiscal year, largely on the back of two large renewable-energy facilities.

2. Corporate Underwriting Modernisation - Project ORION

Following the diagnostic commissioned in February, the group formally approved launch of the corporate underwriting modernisation initiative, internally named Project ORION. The diagnostic confirmed that policy-exception handling and manual documentation checks together account for the majority of elapsed TAT beyond the credit committee's own decisioning time.

Pilot scope: 5 branches - Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Ahmedabad corporate banking teams.

Baseline captured for pilot branches: standard-case TAT 9.5 days; exception-case TAT 15.2 days.

Target: reduce pilot-branch standard-case TAT to 6 days within the pilot window (target date: June 2026).

3. Discussion

Kavya Iyer flagged that pilot success will depend heavily on RM adoption of the new digital checklist tool, which requires a change in how proposals are first logged.

Neeraj Bhatia asked that the pilot branches be given adequate training lead time before go-live metrics are judged.

Rohan Desai asked for exception-routing logic to be reviewed by Risk before go-live to ensure no policy checks are silently dropped.

4. Decisions

Project ORION pilot approved for go-live from 20 April 2026 in the five nominated branches.

Risk to sign off on exception-routing logic prior to go-live.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Full underwriting bottleneck diagnostic findings - detailed report circulated separately (closed as a standing item; findings incorporated into ORION scope above).

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

Pipeline held steady at Rs 3,750 Cr across 46 accounts. Sanctions for March closed at Rs 1,020 Cr, the strongest month this fiscal year, largely on the back of two large renewable-energy facilities.

2. Corporate Underwriting Modernisation - Project ORION

Following the diagnostic commissioned in February, the group formally approved launch of the corporate underwriting modernisation initiative, internally named Project ORION. The diagnostic confirmed that policy-exception handling and manual documentation checks together account for the majority of elapsed TAT beyond the credit committee's own decisioning time.

Pilot scope: 5 branches - Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Ahmedabad corporate banking teams.

Baseline captured for pilot branches: standard-case TAT 9.5 days; exception-case TAT 15.2 days.

Target: reduce pilot-branch standard-case TAT to 6 days within the pilot window (target date: June 2026).

Kavya Iyer appointed pilot owner; Sameer Kapoor and Amit Sethi as credit/operations sponsors.

Scope includes a digital document checklist, auto-validation of standard financial covenants, and a revised exception-routing workflow.

3. Discussion

Kavya Iyer flagged that pilot success will depend heavily on RM adoption of the new digital checklist tool, which requires a change in how proposals are first logged.

Neeraj Bhatia asked that the pilot branches be given adequate training lead time before go-live metrics are judged.

Rohan Desai asked for exception-routing logic to be reviewed by Risk before go-live to ensure no policy checks are silently dropped.

4. Decisions

Project ORION pilot approved for go-live from 20 April 2026 in the five nominated branches.

Risk to sign off on exception-routing logic prior to go-live.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Full underwriting bottleneck diagnostic findings - detailed report circulated separately (closed as a standing item; findings incorporated into ORION scope above).

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

The wholesale pipeline improved to Rs 3,600 Cr across 44 accounts (Jan: Rs 3,200 Cr / 40 accounts), driven largely by renewed activity in the infrastructure and light manufacturing segments. Sanctions for the month stood at Rs 890 Cr against a target of Rs 950 Cr.

2. Credit Turnaround Time (TAT)

Average TAT for standard corporate proposals was 9.4 days against the internal target of 6 days (Jan: 9.6 days). Sameer Kapoor noted the improvement is marginal and not yet statistically meaningful. Approximately 18% of proposals were returned to the originating RM at least once for documentation rework, which the group agreed is a material contributor to elapsed TAT.

3. Discussion

Neeraj Bhatia flagged that RM teams are spending disproportionate time re-collating financial statements and KYC annexures rather than on credit structuring itself.

Amit Sethi presented a preliminary breakdown showing exception-flagged proposals take nearly 60% longer than clean proposals end-to-end.

Rohan Desai cautioned against diluting policy checks purely to compress TAT; asked that any diagnostic separate genuine risk-driven delay from process friction.

Group agreed a formal diagnostic of underwriting bottlenecks is required before deciding on any technology or process intervention.

4. Decisions

Commission a structured TAT diagnostic covering the last two quarters of proposals, to be jointly led by Credit and Credit Operations.

Neeraj Bhatia to nominate two RM teams (one metro, one non-metro) for a time-and-motion study.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Root-cause analysis of credit TAT (raised in January MBR) - in progress, folded into the new diagnostic exercise.

Digitisation options paper for corporate underwriting - deferred to March, pending diagnostic findings.

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

Pipeline held steady at Rs 3,750 Cr across 46 accounts. Sanctions for March closed at Rs 1,020 Cr, the strongest month this fiscal year, largely on the back of two large renewable-energy facilities.

2. Corporate Underwriting Modernisation - Project ORION

Following the diagnostic commissioned in February, the group formally approved launch of the corporate underwriting modernisation initiative, internally named Project ORION. The diagnostic confirmed that policy-exception handling and manual documentation checks together account for the majority of elapsed TAT beyond the credit committee's own decisioning time.

Pilot scope: 5 branches - Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Ahmedabad corporate banking teams.

Baseline captured for pilot branches: standard-case TAT 9.5 days; exception-case TAT 15.2 days.

Target: reduce pilot-branch standard-case TAT to 6 days within the pilot window (target date: June 2026).

Kavya Iyer appointed pilot owner; Sameer Kapoor and Amit Sethi as credit/operations sponsors.

Scope includes a digital document checklist, auto-validation of standard financial covenants, and a revised exception-routing workflow.

3. Discussion

Kavya Iyer flagged that pilot success will depend heavily on RM adoption of the new digital checklist tool, which requires a change in how proposals are first logged.

Neeraj Bhatia asked that the pilot branches be given adequate training lead time before go-live metrics are judged.

Rohan Desai asked for exception-routing logic to be reviewed by Risk before go-live to ensure no policy checks are silently dropped.

4. Decisions

Project ORION pilot approved for go-live from 20 April 2026 in the five nominated branches.

Risk to sign off on exception-routing logic prior to go-live.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Full underwriting bottleneck diagnostic findings - detailed report circulated separately (closed as a standing item; findings incorporated into ORION scope above).

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

10 May 2026

1. Business Performance

The wholesale pipeline improved to Rs 3,600 Cr across 44 accounts (Jan: Rs 3,200 Cr / 40 accounts), driven largely by renewed activity in the infrastructure and light manufacturing segments. Sanctions for the month stood at Rs 890 Cr against a target of Rs 950 Cr.

2. Credit Turnaround Time (TAT)

Average TAT for standard corporate proposals was 9.4 days against the internal target of 6 days (Jan: 9.6 days). Sameer Kapoor noted the improvement is marginal and not yet statistically meaningful. Approximately 18% of proposals were returned to the originating RM at least once for documentation rework, which the group agreed is a material contributor to elapsed TAT.

3. Discussion

Neeraj Bhatia flagged that RM teams are spending disproportionate time re-collating financial statements and KYC annexures rather than on credit structuring itself.

Amit Sethi presented a preliminary breakdown showing exception-flagged proposals take nearly 60% longer than clean proposals end-to-end.

Rohan Desai cautioned against diluting policy checks purely to compress TAT; asked that any diagnostic separate genuine risk-driven delay from process friction.

Group agreed a formal diagnostic of underwriting bottlenecks is required before deciding on any technology or process intervention.

4. Decisions

Commission a structured TAT diagnostic covering the last two quarters of proposals, to be jointly led by Credit and Credit Operations.

Neeraj Bhatia to nominate two RM teams (one metro, one non-metro) for a time-and-motion study.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Root-cause analysis of credit TAT (raised in January MBR) - in progress, folded into the new diagnostic exercise.

Digitisation options paper for corporate underwriting - deferred to March, pending diagnostic findings.

Minutes of Meeting

Wholesale Banking - Monthly Business Review

12 August 2026

1. Business Performance

Pipeline grew to Rs 3,900 Cr across 47 accounts. April sanctions closed at Rs 940 Cr. Fee income from trade and cash management products was up 6% month-on-month.

2. Project ORION - Pilot Results (5 weeks)

Standard-case proposals are showing a clear and encouraging improvement. Exception cases have improved only marginally and remain the primary drag on overall TAT.

3. Discussion

Neeraj Bhatia raised concern that a meaningful number of proposals are being flagged as 'exceptions' for what he characterised as minor or technical deviations, pushing them into the slower manual track unnecessarily.

Sameer Kapoor pushed back, stating that exception flags reflect genuine policy deviations that require credit judgement and should not be diluted purely to improve a TAT metric.

Amit Sethi noted that a portion of the exception-case delay is attributable to incomplete documentation at first submission, requiring at least one round of rework in most cases.

Ananya Mehra asked for a joint review of exception criteria rather than a unilateral change by either side, given the disagreement between Business and Credit.

Arvind Rao asked that the review distinguish clearly between (a) cases that are exceptions due to genuine risk factors and (b) cases that are exceptions purely due to process or documentation gaps.

4. Decisions

Constitute a joint working group - Credit, Corporate Banking and Digital Transformation - to review exception-flagging criteria and recommend refinements.

Working group to report back at the October MBR.

5. Action Items

6. Open / Carry-Forward Items

Business-Credit alignment on exception criteria - unresolved, escalated to joint working group above.

body:
From: Bharat Rungta bharat.rungta@rbl.bank.in
Sent: 13 April 2026 19:40
To: R Subramaniakumar r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Cc: Vikram Sriram vikram.sriram@rbl.bank.in; Atharva Karkhanis atharva.karkhanis@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Wholesale Banking - April Review | Minutes
 
Hi all,
 
Notes from yesterday's Wholesale Banking review for the record.
 
Attendees: R Subramaniakumar, Bharat Rungta (chair), Vikram Sriram, Atharva Karkhanis
 
1. Business performance
 
* Wholesale loan book at Rs 42,300 Cr, YoY growth 14%, broadly in line with budget.
* Pipeline at Rs 3,200 Cr across 40 accounts - softer than we'd like; new client acquisition has lagged budget through Q4, mainly in the mid-corporate segment.
* March sanctions closed at Rs 780 Cr.
 
2. Credit TAT
 
* Average TAT for standard corporate proposals was 9.6 days against our internal target of 6 days.
* This is the first time we've formally flagged TAT as a constraint on growth rather than just an operating metric - a few RMs have cited it as a reason prospects have gone to competitors.
* No granular breakdown available yet on where the time is actually going.
 
3. Discussion
 
* Vikram flagged that any push to compress TAT should not come at the cost of policy checks.
* Atharva noted the Credit team hasn't had a chance to look at this in a structured way - most read is anecdotal so far.
* R Subramaniakumar asked for a proper root-cause analysis rather than incremental fixes - wants to understand whether this is a policy issue, a documentation issue, a resourcing issue, or all three, before we commit to anything.
 
4. Decisions
 
* Commission a root-cause analysis of credit TAT - Credit and Credit Operations to lead, findings to be brought back within 4-6 weeks.
 
5. Actions
 
* Vikram Sriram / Atharva Karkhanis: scope and kick off TAT root-cause analysis - due 10 May
* Atharva Karkhanis: share RM-level anecdotal feedback on TAT-related pipeline losses - due 24 Apr
* Bharat Rungta: circulate revised pipeline targets for Q1 FY27 - due 20 Apr
 
Will circulate the diagnostic scope once Vikram and Atharva have firmed it up.
 
Regards,
Bharat Rungta
Head - Wholesale Banking
RBL Bank

subject: Lumière Credit Card adoption metrics
body:
From: Vikram
To: R. Subramaniakumar
Cc: Bikram Yadav; Atharva
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026, 09:12
Subject: RE: Lumière Credit Card adoption metrics
Sir,
Summary for the Board conversation: we've issued about 500 cards, and roughly 40% are active. Of that active base, around half are swiping 4-5 times a month or more — so the engaged core is smaller than the headline number, and worth stating plainly rather than leading with 500. Concierge and the free hotel stay are genuinely being used by several of these active customers, which is a good early signal on the experiential side. Reward redemption hasn't picked up yet, but Bikram's view is that's expected given how young the card still is, not a design problem.
On cross-sell — this is a genuine yes. Bikram confirms we're actively coordinating with BBRL and Retail Assets, and this cohort is being treated as a priority customer set. The one gap is that referrals are still offline; a squad is being stood up to build proper online service and enquiry journeys across liabilities and assets for this base.
Vikram

From: Bikram Yadav
To: Vikram; R. Subramaniakumar
Cc: Atharva
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026, 07:40
Subject: RE: Lumière Credit Card adoption metrics
Vikram, RS —
Confirming the numbers Atharva's shared: ~500 cards issued, ~40% active, and of that active base roughly half are swiping 4-5 times a month or more. I'd read this as a healthy early core rather than a concern — concierge and free hotel stay usage among active customers backs that up. Reward redemption being flat right now is consistent with the card's age; I wouldn't over-index on that yet.
On cross-sell — yes, this is live and a priority for us. We're coordinating directly with BBRL and RA product teams on referrals for standalone Lumière holders. It's offline today, which is the honest gap, so we're forming a squad specifically to build online service and enquiry journeys so this doesn't stay a manual, RM-dependent process.
Bikram

From: Atharva
To: Vikram; R. Subramaniakumar
Cc: Bikram Yadav
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026, 20:03
Subject: RE: Lumière Credit Card adoption metrics
Vikram, RS, Bikram —
On activation — we're at about 500 cards issued, with ~40% currently active. Within that active 40%, roughly half are swiping 4-5 times a month or more, so the truly engaged base is closer to 20% of total issuance. Concierge and the complimentary hotel stay are the two features seeing real uptake among active customers. Reward redemption hasn't materialised yet — Bikram, your call on whether that's simply the card being early days, but wanted to flag it as a feature that's live and paid for but not yet delivering visible value to customers.
On cross-sell for standalone holders — Bikram can confirm, but my understanding is we are actively working with BBRL and Retail Assets, with this cohort flagged as priority. Referrals are currently offline; a squad is being formed to stitch together online journeys for liability and asset products for this base.
Atharva

From: Vikram
To: Atharva
Cc: Bikram Yadav
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026, 10:18
Subject: Fwd: Lumière Credit Card adoption metrics
Atharva,
RS wants three things: activation and usage split — ideally feature-level, not just headline card count; cross-sell status for standalone Lumière holders into SA/CA/TD and assets like mortgage or premium vehicle finance; and how active the base really is on features like concierge and hotel stays versus rewards.
Bikram — copying you as this touches your business directly; would help to get your read alongside Atharva's data.
Vikram

From: R. Subramaniakumar
To: Vikram
Cc: Bikram Yadav
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026, 08:55
Subject: Lumière Credit Card adoption metrics
Vikram,
Second thing I want visibility on: of the customers who have Lumière, how many are actually active, and are they using the full feature set or just carrying the card around? Separately — for the ones who took Lumière standalone, are we cross-selling into liabilities and retail assets, or is it sitting as an isolated card relationship?
Bikram — adding you, this is your business to weigh in on directly.
RS
 
Thanks and Regards
 
Tanishq Chourishi 
Manager
Alvarez & Marsal India Private Limited
One World Center
Unit 601/602, 6th Floor, Tower 2A
Off Senapati Bapat Marg, Lower Parel
Mumbai 400 013

subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view
body:
All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

Bharat,

- Product CA: Rs 5,972 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 9,625 Cr. Gap Rs 3,653 Cr.
- Product SA: Rs 1,238 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 1,411 Cr. Gap Rs 173 Cr.

Ashrut

CA balances build in the last ten days of a quarter - they always have. Comparing a mid-month position to a quarter-end target will always show a gap this size.

Bharat

From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

R Subramaniakumar

subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view
body:
Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

R Subramaniakumar
 

'

=== Message 4 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-4e832afc332ec186bbdbe7100e5d7caa
Date: 09 September 2026 10:15
From: sandeep.nair@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

=== Message 5 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-403113e85aa47b6e996a3f7f87a5e33b
Date: 09 September 2026 16:05
From: aman.gupta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Sandeep,
 
On the decline - I'd put it at roughly Rs 13,000 Cr since March rather than the h=adline number, because the Rs 3,000 Cr co-operative bank term deposit transfer to Retail is an internal reclassification, not an outflow. Worth being precise on that in the pack or we'll be asked about it.
 
On the assumption itself I'd defer to Bharat on how much of the base he expects to rebuild by the 30th. Happy to run it both ways.

Thanks and Regards
 
Tanishq Chourishi

Bharat

R Subramaniakumar

Date: 27 August 2026 17:30
From: ashrut.binani@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
Ahead of the September review, the target-versus-actual position on wholesale CA and SA as it stands:
 
- Product CA: Rs 5,972 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 9,625 Cr. Gap Rs 3,653 Cr.
- Product SA: Rs 1,238 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 1,411 Cr. Gap Rs 173 Cr.
 
The CA gap is the one that matters. FIGU CA alone is Rs 330 Cr against a target of Rs 1,400 Cr, and Liabilities/New Economy is Rs 1,066 Cr against Rs 2,000 Cr.
 
Need a view from WB on whether these targets are still achievable by the 30th, since I have to reflect something in the MIS.
 
Ashrut

=== Message 11 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-6b2f61dc83e5a499e957dfbefbab0eef
Date: 28 August 2026 09:50
From: bharat.rungta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Ashrut,
 
CA balances build in the last ten days of a quarter - they always have. Comparing a mid-month position to a quarter-end target will always show a gap this size.
 
We'll be closer than that number suggests. I'd rather not revise the target with four weeks still to run.
 
Bharat

=== Message 12 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-2320b0ee85d5587d4cfa403e8cb8241b
Date: 28 August 2026 19:20
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
"It builds at quarter end" is an explanation of the pattern, not a plan to close a Rs 3,653 Cr gap.
 
Tell me which names are going to fund it and what each is worth. If the answer is that we're relying on the same NBFC balances that came off in August, then we don't have a plan, we have a hope.
 
R Subramaniakumar

'

thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

=== Message 2 of 12 ===

Date: 04 September 2026 15:10
From: deep.khatri@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack
body:
Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

=== Message 2 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-85ab3a51664d55d07aca811e178a3901
Date: 04 September 2026 15:10
From: deep.khatri@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

Bharat

Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
Ahead of the September review, the target-versus-actual position on wholesale CA and SA as it stands:
 
- Product CA: Rs 5,972 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 9,625 Cr. Gap Rs 3,653 Cr.
- Product SA: Rs 1,238 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 1,411 Cr. Gap Rs 173 Cr.
 
The CA gap is the one that matters. FIGU CA alone is Rs 330 Cr against a target of Rs 1,400 Cr, and Liabilities/New Economy is Rs 1,066 Cr against Rs 2,000 Cr.
 
Need a view from WB on whether these targets are still achievable by the 30th, since I have to reflect something in the MIS.
 
Ashrut

=== Message 11 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-6b2f61dc83e5a499e957dfbefbab0eef
Date: 28 August 2026 09:50
From: bharat.rungta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Ashrut,
 
CA balances build in the last ten days of a quarter - they always have. Comparing a mid-month position to a quarter-end target will always show a gap this size.
 
We'll be closer than that number suggests. I'd rather not revise the target with four weeks still to run.
 
Bharat

=== Message 12 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-2320b0ee85d5587d4cfa403e8cb8241b
Date: 28 August 2026 19:20
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
"It builds at quarter end" is an explanation of the pattern, not a plan to close a Rs 3,653 Cr gap.
 
Tell me which names are going to fund it and what each is worth. If the answer is that we're relying on the same NBFC balances that came off in August, then we don't have a plan, we have a hope.
 
R Subramaniakumar

'

thread_subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view
thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

=== Message 2 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-85ab3a51664d55d07aca811e178a3901
Date: 04 September 2026 15:10
From: deep.khatri@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

=== Message 3 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-5c801bba1f493813c7bdaa41c9850c70
Date: 04 September 2026 20:45
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

So we publish a daily balance sheet to the top of this bank, and we cannot tell me how much of our wholesale funding is callable overnight.
 
Rohan's question is the right one. Get me the answer before the 18th, manual or otherwise.
 
R Subramaniakumar
 

'

=== Message 4 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-4e832afc332ec186bbdbe7100e5d7caa
Date: 09 September 2026 10:15
From: sandeep.nair@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

=== Message 5 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-403113e85aa47b6e996a3f7f87a5e33b
Date: 09 September 2026 16:05
From: aman.gupta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Sandeep,
 
On the decline - I'd put it at roughly Rs 13,000 Cr since March rather than the h=adline number, because the Rs 3,000 Cr co-operative bank term deposit transfer to Retail is an internal reclassification, not an outflow. Worth being precise on that in the pack or we'll be asked about it.
 
On the assumption itself I'd defer to Bharat on how much of the base he expects to rebuild by the 30th. Happy to run it both ways.

Thanks and Regards
 
Tanishq Chourishi

Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
Ahead of the September review, the target-versus-actual position on wholesale CA and SA as it stands:
 
- Product CA: Rs 5,972 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 9,625 Cr. Gap Rs 3,653 Cr.
- Product SA: Rs 1,238 Cr against a Sep-26 target of Rs 1,411 Cr. Gap Rs 173 Cr.
 
The CA gap is the one that matters. FIGU CA alone is Rs 330 Cr against a target of Rs 1,400 Cr, and Liabilities/New Economy is Rs 1,066 Cr against Rs 2,000 Cr.
 
Need a view from WB on whether these targets are still achievable by the 30th, since I have to reflect something in the MIS.
 
Ashrut

=== Message 11 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-6b2f61dc83e5a499e957dfbefbab0eef
Date: 28 August 2026 09:50
From: bharat.rungta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Ashrut,
 
CA balances build in the last ten days of a quarter - they always have. Comparing a mid-month position to a quarter-end target will always show a gap this size.
 
We'll be closer than that number suggests. I'd rather not revise the target with four weeks still to run.
 
Bharat

=== Message 12 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-2320b0ee85d5587d4cfa403e8cb8241b
Date: 28 August 2026 19:20
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
"It builds at quarter end" is an explanation of the pattern, not a plan to close a Rs 3,653 Cr gap.
 
Tell me which names are going to fund it and what each is worth. If the answer is that we're relying on the same NBFC balances that came off in August, then we don't have a plan, we have a hope.
 
R Subramaniakumar

'

thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

=== Message 2 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-85ab3a51664d55d07aca811e178a3901
Date: 04 September 2026 15:10
From: deep.khatri@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

R Subramaniakumar

Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

thread_subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view
thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

=== Message 2 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-85ab3a51664d55d07aca811e178a3901
Date: 04 September 2026 15:10
From: deep.khatri@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

=== Message 3 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-5c801bba1f493813c7bdaa41c9850c70
Date: 04 September 2026 20:45
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

So we publish a daily balance sheet to the top of this bank, and we cannot tell me how much of our wholesale funding is callable overnight.
 
Rohan's question is the right one. Get me the answer before the 18th, manual or otherwise.
 
R Subramaniakumar
 

'

=== Message 4 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-4e832afc332ec186bbdbe7100e5d7caa
Date: 09 September 2026 10:15
From: sandeep.nair@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

=== Message 5 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-403113e85aa47b6e996a3f7f87a5e33b
Date: 09 September 2026 16:05
From: aman.gupta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Sandeep,
 
On the decline - I'd put it at roughly Rs 13,000 Cr since March rather than the h=adline number, because the Rs 3,000 Cr co-operative bank term deposit transfer to Retail is an internal reclassification, not an outflow. Worth being precise on that in the pack or we'll be asked about it.
 
On the assumption itself I'd defer to Bharat on how much of the base he expects to rebuild by the 30th. Happy to run it both ways.

Thanks and Regards
 
Tanishq Chourishi

Ashrut

Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Ashrut,
 
CA balances build in the last ten days of a quarter - they always have. Comparing a mid-month position to a quarter-end target will always show a gap this size.
 
We'll be closer than that number suggests. I'd rather not revise the target with four weeks still to run.
 
Bharat

=== Message 12 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-2320b0ee85d5587d4cfa403e8cb8241b
Date: 28 August 2026 19:20
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Sep-26 CA/SA targets - WB view required

Bharat,
 
"It builds at quarter end" is an explanation of the pattern, not a plan to close a Rs 3,653 Cr gap.
 
Tell me which names are going to fund it and what each is worth. If the answer is that we're relying on the same NBFC balances that came off in August, then we don't have a plan, we have a hope.
 
R Subramaniakumar

thread_subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view
thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan

=== Message 2 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-85ab3a51664d55d07aca811e178a3901
Date: 04 September 2026 15:10
From: deep.khatri@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

Rohan,
 
Can pull the top-twenty by balance from the daily pack, but a caveat: the client-wise cuts we publish daily are top-five movers, not a full concentration view. A proper tenor and callability split would need to come from the core system rather than the Tableau extract, and that's a manual exercise at present.
 
Also worth noting the Rs 3,000 Cr of co-operative bank term deposits that moved from Govt Banking to Retail - that shows as a reduction in our numbers but it hasn't left the bank. Any concentration read needs to strip that out.
 
Will have something by end of next week.
 
Deep

=== Message 3 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-5c801bba1f493813c7bdaa41c9850c70
Date: 04 September 2026 20:45
From: r.subramaniakumar@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

So we publish a daily balance sheet to the top of this bank, and we cannot tell me how much of our wholesale funding is callable overnight.
 
Rohan's question is the right one. Get me the answer before the 18th, manual or otherwise.
 
R Subramaniakumar
 

'

=== Message 4 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-4e832afc332ec186bbdbe7100e5d7caa
Date: 09 September 2026 10:15
From: sandeep.nair@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Aman, Bharat,
 
Need to lock the funding cost assumption for the Q3 NIM pack this week.
 
The issue is straightforward. Wholesale deposits have run down materially sinc= March while the wholesale book has continued to grow. We've been plugging the difference with retail term deposits and market borrowing, both of which are priced above what the FIGU and corporate balances were costing us.
 
If the wholesale deposit base doesn't rebuild by the 30th, the blended cost of funds on the WB book goes up by something in the order of 15-20 bps into Q3. That is not a rounding difference at this book size.
 
What deposit number should I build in?
 
Sandeep

=== Message 5 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-403113e85aa47b6e996a3f7f87a5e33b
Date: 09 September 2026 16:05
From: aman.gupta@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Q3 funding cost assumption for the NIM pack

Sandeep,
 
On the decline - I'd put it at roughly Rs 13,000 Cr since March rather than the h=adline number, because the Rs 3,000 Cr co-operative bank term deposit transfer to Retail is an internal reclassification, not an outflow. Worth being precise on that in the pack or we'll be asked about it.
 
On the assumption itself I'd defer to Bharat on how much of the base he expects to rebuild by the 30th. Happy to run it both ways.

Thanks and Regards
 
Tanishq Chourishi

Bharat

R Subramaniakumar

Ashrut

Ashrut,
 
CA balances build in the last ten days of a quarter - they always have. Comparing a mid-month position to a quarter-end target will always show a gap this size.

Bharat

thread_raw_content:
=== Message 1 of 12 ===
Message-ID: pg-7f3de71405b56a5c63c85fca681bed86
Date: 03 September 2026 11:25
From: rohan.desai@rbl.bank.in
Subject: Concentration in wholesale deposits - risk view

All,
 
Raising this from a risk rather than a business angle.
 
FIGU deposits have gone from Rs 11,140 Cr at 31-Mar to Rs 2,719 Cr at 17-Aug. That is a Rs 8,421 Cr reduction in one segment in under five months. On a single day in August, two entities in the same group accounted for Rs 323 Cr of outflow.
 
My concern isn't the level, it's the dependency. I don't have a clear picture of how much of the wholesale deposit base sits with the top twenty names, or how much of that is overnight and callable. Without that I can't give a view on whether this is a manageable rundown or a concentration exposure.
 
Requesting a top-twenty depositor dependency view with tenor and callability.
 
Rohan
